lines.text: This is your token board book. Four laminated pages are bound on the left, with a tab for each: Choices, Targets, Board, and Tokens.
lines.screen: The closed book lies on a table with its four labelled tabs showing on the right, then it opens to the first page.

lines.text: Page one is the Choices page. Show it to your learner before the task begins. Every picture should be something your learner values.
lines.screen: The Choices page fills the frame, with six choice cards on its six boxes.

lines.text: Your learner looks over the pictures and picks one to work for. Prompt gently if needed.
lines.screen: The learner's small hand moves across the cards, points at one, then pinches it and lifts it off the page.

lines.text: Page two is the Targets page. Here, you choose what to teach: a new skill, or a replacement behavior from the behavior plan.
lines.screen: The page turns to the Targets page, with six teaching target cards on its boxes.

lines.text: Choose one target at a time. Agree with the other adults on exactly what counts, so everyone gives tokens for the same thing.
lines.screen: The teacher's hand, with a shirt cuff, picks the first target card and lifts it off the page.

lines.text: Page three is the Board. Place the target under First, and the chosen item under Then. Now your learner can see the plan: first the work, then the item.
lines.screen: The page turns to the Board; the target card goes into the First box and the chosen item card into the Then box.

lines.text: Page four is the Tokens page, where the tokens wait. The empty slots on the Board show your learner how many are left.
lines.screen: The Tokens page appears beside the Board with its tokens in their boxes, and the empty token slots on the Board are highlighted.

lines.text: Before you start, decide how much behavior earns one token. In this example, your learner earns a token for every two minutes of working.
lines.screen: A note over the Board and Tokens page reads: one token for every two minutes of working.

lines.text: Now start the session. Point to the board: first work, then the item. The ring shows each interval, sped up for this video.
lines.screen: A timer ring appears beside the Board, labelled as sped up, and starts to fill.

lines.text: The interval is over, and your learner kept working. Give a token right away, with brief, specific praise, like "Great working!" Your learner places it in the first slot.
lines.screen: As the ring completes, the teacher's hand takes a token from the Tokens page and it goes into the first slot, with a speech bubble: Great working!

lines.text: If your learner was not working during an interval, no token is given. Stay calm and simply start the next interval.
lines.screen: The ring completes while the learner is off task; no token moves, and the ring starts again from zero.

lines.text: Each interval of working earns another token, given right away with a few words of praise. The board fills up, one slot at a time.
lines.screen: The intervals run faster now; token after token goes into the next slot, each with a short bubble of praise.

lines.text: This last token looks different: it is the terminal token. It shows your learner that the board is finished and the item comes next.
lines.screen: The last token, with its own picture and an orange double border, goes into the last slot, which carries an orange ring.

lines.text: The last token fills the board. Your learner has earned the item they chose.
lines.screen: The last token goes into the last slot, and every slot on the Board is full.

lines.text: The board is full, so make the exchange right away, especially while the board is new. Give the Then item for the time you planned.
lines.screen: The Then card lifts and grows, and the teacher's hand passes it to the learner's hand, with a label for the planned time with the item.

lines.text: When the time is up, put the tokens back on the Tokens page and the cards back on their pages. Then your learner chooses again, for the next round.
lines.screen: The tokens go back to the Tokens page, the two cards return to their pages, and the book turns back to the Choices page.

lines.text: A few tips. Make tokens valuable first: give one and exchange it right away, several times. Start with a small requirement and raise it slowly; if the behavior falls apart, go back a step. Keep the item available only through the board.
lines.screen: Three short tips appear one by one beside the book: pair the tokens first, start small and raise slowly, the item only through the board.

lines.text: That's the whole cycle: choose, set the target, earn the tokens, and exchange. The back of each page tells you more.
lines.screen: The book closes on the table with its four tabs showing.
